title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rope-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Reduce token-level latency and improve GPU throughput for long-context workloads by upgrading the attention kernels to the latest FlashAttentionV2 variant and folding fused rotary/rope ops into a single fused kernel where possible. This PR also tightens scheduling heuristics for continuous batching and improves KV-cache alignment to avoid extra memcpy operations. Summary of changes: 1) Add FlashAttnV2 fused kernel path with rope/rotary fusion and qkv-layout optimizations; 2) Introduce a new kernel selection decision in the runtime that picks fused flashattn when sequence length and head dims match the heuristics; 3) Update KV cache memory layout to align tensors to 256-byte boundaries and avoid per-request reallocs; 4) Continuous batching improvements: better coalescing policy for interleaved chat workloads and a small change to windowing to reduce tail latency; 5) Microbenchmarks and regression tests added; 6) Docs and runtime feature flag (RUNTIME_USE_FV2_FUSED_ATTn) for safe rollout. Checklist:
- [x] Kernel integration and unit tests
- [x] Integration tests on A100 and H100 nodes
- [x] Benchmarks (latency and throughput)
- [x] Feature flag gating for canary rollout
- [x] Documentation and release notes
Implementation notes: The fused kernel implements rotary/rope as an in-kernel transformation prior to softmax and supports both rotary and rope encodings via a compile-time template parameter. The runtime kernel selector evaluates: model.type == transformer && head_dim % 64 == 0 && seq_len >= 64 && batch_size >= 1 && device_compute_capability >= 80. If selected, we route through the new fused path which reduces memory traffic by ~22% in our microbenchmarks. KV cache layout changes remove a memcpy in the hot path by changing how we append key/value slices; this required careful pinning and a fallback for older saved cache formats. Rollout plan: gated behind RUNTIME_USE_FV2_FUSED_ATTn, start canary on Dedicated pools in us-west-2 with 5% traffic, monitor latency P95 and generation throughput for regressions. Benchmarks: On H100 (bfloat16), for a 32k context benchmark with batch=4 we measured token throughput increase +38% and P95 latency drop 21% compared to previous flashattn path. Safety: feature-flagged, falls back to prior kernels on incompatibility, and adds a health check that verifies numerical agreement within 1e-4 for sampling seeds used in our eval harness. Related: ENG-3452 (attention kernel upgrades), ENG-3487 (kv-cache alignment), SUP-9123 (customer-reported tail latency incident).

review_comments: Benji Martinez: Could you add a fallback path for saved KV cache blobs that were written with old padding? I hit an incompatibility when testing on a local snapshot.
Aisha Kapoor: Added a compatibility shim in kv_cache_manager that detects old-format headers and replays into the new aligned buffer without an extra malloc; added unit test.
Clara Zhou: The kernel looks good but please add a small deterministic rng test to ensure numerical parity for sampling with small seed across paths.
Aisha Kapoor: Added deterministic RNG parity test and tolerances. Results are within 1e-4 for sampled logits across 1000 seeds.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaked once on lint -> fixed-cmake formatting; re-ran full CI and all GPU tests passed.
Benji Martinez: Approved after verifying benchmarks on H100 (us-west-2 dedicated pool) show P95 improvement and no regression on short-context workloads.
Clara Zhou: Approved - roll out under feature flag only.
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 fused variant with rope/rotary fusion and qkv layout optimizations leading to up to +38% token throughput on H100 for long-context workloads. Runtime: improved kernel selection heuristics and continuous batching coalescing to reduce tail latency. KV cache: aligned allocations to remove an extra memcpy and improve memory throughput. Rollout: feature-flagged (RUNTIME_USE_FV2_FUSED_ATTn) and canaried.
